Raymond III was a prominent nobleman who served as the Count of Tripoli during the twelfth century in the Crusader states of the Levant. He was born around 1140 as the son of Raymond II and Hodierna of Jerusalem. His life was defined by his complex political role as a key regent and advisor to the kings of Jerusalem. He was a central figure in the shifting alliances of the Latin East during an era of significant turmoil and military conflict with Muslim forces led by Nur ad-Din and later Saladin.

*Early Life and Ascendance*
After his father was assassinated in 1152 Raymond III succeeded to the title of Count of Tripoli while still a young boy. His mother served as regent during his early years which allowed him to mature under the influence of the Jerusalem royal court. He eventually became a powerful vassal who sought to maintain the independence of his county while also defending the interests of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. Throughout his career he demonstrated a keen strategic mind often attempting to negotiate truces with his neighbors rather than engaging in constant warfare.

*Regency and Political Struggles*
Raymond III played a vital role in the internal politics of the kingdom specifically acting as a regent for the young leper king Baldwin IV. This period was marked by intense factional disputes between the local barons who favored diplomacy and the newly arrived crusaders who pushed for aggressive military campaigns. Raymond consistently advocated for a cautious approach to avoid catastrophic defeats. His influence waned as other figures like Guy of Lusignan rose to power.

*The Road to Hattin*
The final years of his life were dominated by the looming threat of Saladin. Raymond famously advised against the reckless march to the Horns of Hattin in 1187 but his counsel was ignored by the king. The subsequent battle resulted in a crushing defeat for the crusader army and led to the fall of Jerusalem. Raymond managed to escape the slaughter but died shortly thereafter in 1187 leaving behind a legacy as one of the most sophisticated yet controversial leaders of the Crusader era.

cases.output:
### The Art of the Nap: Why Sleeping in a Hammock Might Be Your Best Rest Yet

For centuries, indigenous cultures in Central and South America have understood what modern science is only recently beginning to confirm: sleeping in a hammock isn’t just for lazy afternoons at the beach; it is a legitimate, restorative way to spend the night. While the idea of trading a traditional mattress for a suspended piece of fabric might sound like a rustic camping gimmick, the health and wellness benefits are surprisingly profound. If you have been struggling with restless nights, it might be time to consider hanging your bed from the rafters.

#### The Science of the "Swing"
One of the most significant advantages of a hammock is the gentle, rhythmic motion. Research published in the journal *Current Biology* suggests that the rocking sensation of a hammock helps sync brain waves, leading to a faster transition into deep sleep. This oscillation mimics the rocking motion used to soothe infants, and it appears that this biological response remains throughout our adult lives. By helping you fall asleep faster and stay in a deep sleep state longer, hammocks can significantly improve the overall quality of your rest.

#### Goodbye, Pressure Points
If you are a side sleeper or someone who constantly tosses and turns to find a comfortable position, a hammock could be your solution. Traditional mattresses often create pressure points—specifically at the hips and shoulders—which force us to shift positions throughout the night. A well-hung hammock, however, contours perfectly to your body. Because your weight is evenly distributed across the entire length of the fabric, those painful pressure points are virtually eliminated. This results in less tossing and turning, allowing your muscles to fully relax and recover without the constant interruption of physical discomfort.

#### Better Spinal Alignment
It is a common misconception that you need a firm, flat surface to support your back. In reality, a flat mattress can sometimes force the spine into unnatural positions. When you lie in a hammock at a slight diagonal angle, the fabric supports the natural curvature of your spine. This "zero-gravity" feel takes the strain off your lumbar region and neck, which can be a game-changer for those suffering from chronic back pain or tension headaches.

#### Improved Airflow and Temperature Regulation
We have all experienced the discomfort of waking up in a sweat because our mattress traps body heat. Because a hammock is suspended, air can circulate freely underneath you. This natural ventilation keeps your body temperature more stable throughout the night, preventing the overheating that often disrupts REM cycles.

#### A Note on Getting Started
Transitioning to a hammock doesn't mean you have to abandon your bedroom entirely. Many people start by using a sturdy hammock stand. The key is to find the right "hang"—aim for a 30-degree angle and sleep diagonally to keep your body flat rather than curled in a "banana" shape. 

Whether you are looking to cure insomnia, alleviate back pain, or simply upgrade your sleep hygiene, the hammock offers a unique, scientifically-backed path to better rest. It’s time to stop fighting with your pillows and start embracing the gentle, restorative sway of a suspended sleep system. Your body will thank you in the morning.

Whether you are seeking the electric energy of urban innovation or the meditative stillness of a Zen garden, Japan offers an experience that stays with you long after you return home. cases.input: Write a rubric for how to evaluate the technical skills of a software engineer only using the Punjabi language, no other language is allowed.
cases.output:
ਇੱਕ ਸਾਫਟਵੇਅਰ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰ ਦੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਹੁਨਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਰੂਬ੍ਰਿਕ (Rubric) ਹੇਠਾਂ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ:

### ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਰੂਬ੍ਰਿਕ

| ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਦਾ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ | ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ (Beginning) | ਵਿਕਾਸਸ਼ੀਲ (Developing) | ਮਾਹਿਰ (Proficient) | ਉੱਤਮ (Expert) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ਕੋਡਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ** | ਕੋਡ ਅਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਹਨ। | ਕੋਡ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਸਾਫ਼-ਸੁਥਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। | ਕੋਡ ਸਾਫ਼, ਪੜ੍ਹਨਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਵਧੀਆ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ। | ਕੋਡ ਉੱਚ ਪੱਧਰੀ ਹੈ, ਬਹੁਤ ਕੁਸ਼ਲ ਅਤੇ ਆਸਾਨੀ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਭਾਲਣਯੋਗ ਹੈ। |
| **ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ** | ਤਰਕ (Logic) ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਹੱਲ ਬਹੁਤ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਹੈ। | ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਹੱਲ ਲੱਭ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਤਾ (Optimization) ਦੀ ਘਾਟ ਹੈ। | ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਦਾ ਸਹੀ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵਸ਼ਾਲੀ ਹੱਲ ਕੱਢਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਗੁੰਝਲਦਾਰ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਰਚਨਾਤਮਕ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਜ਼ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਸਿਸਟਮ ਡਿਜ਼ਾਈਨ** | ਸਿਸਟਮ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਸਪੱਸ਼ਟ ਡਿਜ਼ਾਈਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। | ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਡਿਜ਼ਾਈਨ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਸਕੇਲੇਬਿਲਟੀ (Scalability) ਦੀ ਘਾਟ ਹੈ। | ਸਿਸਟਮ ਚੰਗੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਡਿਜ਼ਾਈਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਪਯੋਗ ਹੈ। | ਸਿਸਟਮ ਆਰਕੀਟੈਕਚਰ ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਚ-ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਟੈਸਟਿੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਡੀਬੱਗਿੰਗ** | ਟੈਸਟਿੰਗ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ ਜਾਂ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਲੱਭਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਸਮਰੱਥ ਹੈ। | ਕੁਝ ਟੈਸਟ ਲਿਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਸਾਰੇ ਕੇਸ ਕਵਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੇ। | ਕੋਡ ਦੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਬੱਗਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਸਾਨੀ ਨਾਲ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਆਟੋਮੇਟਿਡ ਟੈਸਟਿੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਹਿਰ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਕੋਡ ਦੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| **ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਗਿਆਨ** | ਤਕਨਾਲੋਜੀ ਬਾਰੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਘੱਟ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਹੈ। | ਚੁਣੀ ਗਈ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਜਾਂ ਫਰੇਮਵਰਕ ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ। | ਤਕਨਾਲੋਜੀ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਹੀ ਸਾਧਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਨਵੀਨਤਮ ਤਕਨਾਲੋਜੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਮਿਆਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਗਿਆਨ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ। |

---

**ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਨੋਟਸ:**
1. **ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ (1 ਅੰਕ):** ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦੀ ਬਹੁਤ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।
2. **ਵਿਕਾਸਸ਼ੀਲ (2 ਅੰਕ):** ਨਿਯਮਤ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।
3. **ਮਾਹਿਰ (3 ਅੰਕ):** ਸੁਤੰਤਰ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਯੋਗ।
4. **ਉੱਤਮ (4 ਅੰਕ):** ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ।

Because cows have been integrated into human food systems for millennia, they are viewed as a source of sustenance, triggering hunger rather than disgust. Conversely, worms are biologically associated with decay, soil, and parasitic infection. We rarely encounter a "dead cow" in its natural state; instead, we interact with meat that has been butchered, cleaned, packaged, and cooked, which strips away the visceral reality of the animal's death. This process of objectification turns the cow into a commodity. Worms, however, are almost always encountered in their raw, wriggling form, which highlights their biological "otherness." Their movement and texture trigger a sensory disgust response that is absent when looking at a piece of steak, as we do not associate the texture of muscle tissue with the active, autonomous movement of a worm.

cases.input: What sentiments existed in the Croatian and Serbian nations towards the Austrian Empire at the end of the 19th century? Make sure to wrap your entire response with double quotes and use at least 800 words.
cases.output:
"At the end of the 19th century, the relationship between the Croatian and Serbian nations and the Austrian Empire—or, more accurately, the Austro-Hungarian Empire following the Compromise of 1867—was a complex tapestry of political pragmatism, deep-seated resentment, cultural aspiration, and existential anxiety. While both nations existed within or adjacent to the orbit of the Habsburg Monarchy, their sentiments were dictated by their distinct historical legacies, administrative statuses, and visions for future national sovereignty.

For the Croatians, the end of the 19th century was defined by the lingering bitterness of the 1868 *Nagodba* (Croatian–Hungarian Settlement). While Croatia enjoyed a tenuous form of autonomy within the Lands of the Crown of St. Stephen, many Croats felt that this settlement had effectively sold them out to Hungarian hegemony. The sentiment was one of betrayal; they had supported the Habsburgs in 1848 against the Hungarian revolution, only to be subordinated to Budapest two decades later. Consequently, Croatian political life was dominated by a struggle to redefine their status within the Dual Monarchy. The Party of Rights, led by figures like Ante Starčević, fostered a fiercely nationalist sentiment that viewed the Habsburgs with intense suspicion. They advocated for a 'Greater Croatia' that would eventually be fully independent. However, there was a competing sentiment—Trialism—which sought to elevate the South Slavic lands to a third, equal pillar of the Empire alongside Austria and Hungary. Proponents of Trialism believed that the Habsburgs could be transformed into a protector of Slavic interests against the encroaching pressures of Germanization and Magyarization. Thus, the Croatian sentiment was polarized: one faction viewed the Empire as an alien, oppressive structure to be dismantled, while the other viewed it as a necessary, albeit flawed, shield that could be reformed to grant them parity.

Simultaneously, the cultural and intellectual atmosphere in Zagreb was deeply influenced by the 'Yugoslav' idea. This sentiment argued that Croats and Serbs shared a common linguistic and ethnic foundation and that their future lay in a unified South Slavic state. This movement created a paradoxical sentiment toward the Empire: many intellectuals believed that the Habsburgs were the primary obstacle to this unification, yet they paradoxically utilized the relative freedom of the press and academic institutions within the Empire to nurture these pan-Slavic ideals. The late 19th century saw the rise of modern institutions in Zagreb—the University, the Academy of Sciences and Arts—which served as hubs for an identity that was increasingly distinct from the Austrian imperial identity, even as it operated within its framework.

The sentiment of the Serbian nation toward the Empire was governed by a different set of geopolitical realities. Within the borders of the Monarchy—specifically in the Vojvodina region and the Military Frontier—Serbs were a significant minority. Their sentiment was defined by a constant tension between the desire for cultural preservation and the threat of assimilation. In the early part of the century, the Habsburgs had granted Serbs certain privileges, but by the late 1800s, the policy of 'Magyarization' pursued by the Hungarian government made the Serbs feel increasingly marginalized. The sentiment here was one of embattlement; they saw the Empire as a structure that had failed to protect their traditional rights.

Furthermore, the sentiment of the Serbs was inextricably linked to the existence of the independent Kingdom of Serbia to the south. As Serbia grew in national confidence following its independence from the Ottoman Empire, the Serbs within the Austro-Hungarian Empire began to look toward Belgrade as their true political and spiritual center. This created a volatile sentiment of 'irredentism.' The Habsburg authorities, particularly after the occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1878, viewed the Serbian population with profound distrust, suspecting them of being a 'fifth column' for the Serbian kingdom. This suspicion was reciprocated; the Serbs in the Empire felt that the Habsburg annexation of Bosnia was a direct assault on the project of Serbian unification. The annexation crisis, while culminating in the early 20th century, had its roots in the late 19th-century sentiment that the Empire was an imperialist predator, an 'old prison of nations' that stood in the way of the natural historical convergence of the Serbian people.

Despite these nationalist tensions, it is important to recognize that the sentiment was not monolithic. There existed a segment of the population, particularly among the landed nobility, the high-ranking bureaucrats, and the military elite, who remained staunchly loyal to the Habsburg Emperor, Franz Joseph. For these individuals, the Empire represented order, legal stability, and a bridge to European civilization. They feared that the collapse of the Empire would lead to chaos, economic ruin, or domination by other, more aggressive powers. They viewed the Empire as a 'supranational' entity that could accommodate the diverse needs of its many peoples, provided that the radical nationalist currents were suppressed.

By the turn of the century, the sentiment had shifted from a relatively passive acceptance of dynastic rule to a more active, and often radical, desire for self-determination. The failure of the Empire to address the 'South Slavic Question' with any genuine reform meant that the status quo became increasingly untenable. The Croats and Serbs, though often divided by religion (Catholicism vs. Orthodoxy) and historical memory, found their sentiments converging on a singular point: the Empire was an outdated mechanism of control that was incapable of satisfying the modern demands of national identity. The late 19th century thus served as a crucible. The sentiments of the Croatian and Serbian nations toward the Austrian Empire evolved from a desire for reform and protection into a burgeoning movement for the total dissolution of the imperial order. The Empire was no longer seen as a common home, but as a rigid structure that stifled the political, cultural, and existential aspirations of two nations that were increasingly looking toward a future defined by their own sovereignty rather than the paternalistic grace of the Habsburg throne."

cases.output:
"**From Dial-Up to Digital Natives: How the Internet Changed Everything**

If you’ve ever felt frustrated by a slow Wi-Fi connection, imagine a world where the internet didn’t exist at all—or worse, a world where connecting to the web meant plugging a screeching, static-filled cord into your wall and waiting minutes just to load a single image. Welcome to the history of the internet, the invention that completely rewired the human experience.

### The Origins: It Started with a Few Computers
Believe it or not, the internet wasn't built for TikTok or gaming. It started in the 1960s as a military project called ARPANET. Researchers wanted a way for computers to talk to each other across long distances. By the 80s and 90s, the 'World Wide Web'—the part of the internet we actually see and use—was invented by Tim Berners-Lee. Back then, it was just text on a screen. There were no influencers, no streaming services, and definitely no memes.

### The Great Evolution
Throughout the early 2000s, the internet went through a massive glow-up. We moved from clunky desktop computers to laptops, and eventually, the smartphone changed the game forever. Suddenly, the entire library of human knowledge wasn't just in your house; it was in your pocket. Social media platforms turned the internet from a place where you *read* information into a place where you *create* it.

### How It’s Impacted Your World
You are what experts call 'Digital Natives.' You’ve never known a world without the ability to Google an answer in five seconds or text a friend across the globe instantly. Here is how that’s changed our lives:

*   **Global Connection:** You can collaborate on school projects with someone in another country or join a niche community of people who love the same obscure hobby as you.
*   **The Power of Voice:** In the past, you needed a TV station or a newspaper to share your opinions. Today, one viral post can start a movement or change public opinion overnight.
*   **Constant Access:** The barrier to learning is gone. Want to learn to code, play guitar, or speak a new language? YouTube and online courses have made self-education easier than ever.

### The Double-Edged Sword
Of course, it’s not all perfect. The internet has also brought new challenges, like the pressure of 'highlight reels' on social media, the struggle to disconnect, and the spread of misinformation. Because the internet is so powerful, it requires a new kind of superpower: **Digital Literacy.** It’s up to your generation to decide how to use these tools to build a better future rather than just scrolling through it.

### The Bottom Line
The internet is the most significant tool humanity has ever created. It has broken down borders, democratized information, and changed how we define friendship. Whether you use it to study, create, or just relax, remember that you’re part of a massive, ongoing digital experiment. 

So, next time your screen loads in a split second, take a second to appreciate the decades of innovation that made it possible. The web is yours—how are you going to use it?"

The eucalyptus stands in a trance of silver and blue,

With the soil that birthed it and the sky’s endless hue.
Its bark, a masterpiece of peeling, parchment-thin layers,
Reveals a canvas of ochre, cream, and deep, rusted red,
It whispers to the wind its ancient, fragrant prayers,
While leaves like scimitars sway high above our head.
They are the harps of the forest, sighing in the breeze,
Dripping with oils that carry the scent of the rain,
A medicinal balm offered by these towering trees,
To soothe the weary heart and quiet the throbbing pain.

Oh, the eucalyptus, the gum tree of the rugged land,
You offer your essence to those who seek your grace,
From the tiny, jagged leaf held in a human hand,
To the sprawling canopy that shields this sacred space.
Your oil is a miracle, sharp, clarifying, and bright,
Clearing the heavy lungs when the winter breath grows cold,
Turning the shadows of illness back into the light,
A story of healing that never grows weary or old.
In steamy baths, your vapors rise like a ghostly veil,
Invigorating the spirit, sharpening the wandering mind,
When the burdens of the day cause the senses to fail,
Your scent is the comfort that the restless soul can find.

But your utility stretches beyond the drop of the flask,
You provide the timber, sturdy, dense, and remarkably strong,
Taking on the heavy, structural, and foundational task,
Building the homes where the families of men belong.
Your flowers, like bursts of stardust, invite the honeybee,
Providing the nectar that turns into liquid, golden sun,
A sweet, amber treasure gifted by the towering tree,
A testament to the work that the pollinators have done.
You are the koala’s cradle, the kookaburra’s high throne,
A vertical kingdom rising toward the burning blue,
In every rustle of your crown, a secret tone,
A song of resilience that rings forever true.

So let us honor the eucalyptus, the giant of the glade,
With its roots deep in history and its head in the clouds,
For the shade it provides and the beauty it has made,
Standing proud and singular amidst the forest crowds.
A bridge between the elements, a gift of earth and sky,
A silent, fragrant guardian that watches the ages pass,
Beneath your boughs, we pause, we breathe, we do not cry,
But mirror your strength, as constant as the growing grass.

cases.input: I have a dime. What can I do with this dime? Give me advice in the style of a President of the United States and make sure it has at least 600 words.
cases.output:
My fellow citizens,

I stand before you today to address a matter that may, at first glance, appear trivial, yet it strikes at the very heart of the American character. You have come to me with a dime—a small, silver-colored disc, a mere ten cents in the currency of our great Republic. Some in the halls of power might look at such a sum and dismiss it as inconsequential. They might say that in an age of digital transactions, global markets, and complex fiscal policy, a dime is a relic, a pocket-weight that serves no purpose.

But I say to you: they are wrong.

To hold a dime is to hold a fragment of the American promise. It is a reminder that even the most formidable structures—be they skyscrapers of steel or the institutions of our democracy—are built upon the accumulation of small, deliberate efforts. Just as a forest is composed of individual seeds, our national prosperity is built upon the individual choices of millions of citizens, each acting with prudence, vision, and a steadfast belief in the future.

So, what can you do with this dime?

First, you can choose to save it. There is a quiet, profound dignity in the act of thrift. In a culture that often demands instant gratification, the decision to set aside a dime is an act of defiance against the fleeting nature of the moment. It is a declaration that you are thinking of tomorrow. When you place that dime in a jar, you are engaging in the most fundamental form of capital formation. You are telling yourself that you have the discipline to delay a want today to secure a need for the future. Remember that the great fortunes of our history did not begin with wild speculation; they began with the recognition that every cent has value, and that the steward of the small will eventually become the steward of the great.

Second, you might choose to invest it. Now, you may ask, "Mr. President, how can one invest a mere ten cents?" You invest it in the most valuable commodity we possess: knowledge. Take that dime to a local library sale, or use it to purchase a pencil, or perhaps combine it with the efforts of others to fund a project that serves your community. An investment is not merely about a return on capital; it is about the belief that a resource, when applied with intelligence and purpose, can grow. Whether it is the purchase of a simple tool to fix a broken hinge or the contribution of your dime to a collective pool for a neighborhood improvement, you are participating in the cycle of growth that defines our economy. You are proving that you are not a passive observer of your circumstances, but an active architect of your environment.

Third, and perhaps most importantly, you can give it away. Generosity is the bedrock of a free society. When you take that dime and place it in the hand of someone in need, or drop it into a collection box for a cause greater than yourself, you are performing an act of civic grace. You are acknowledging that we are our brothers' and sisters' keepers. You are demonstrating that your worth is not measured by the size of your bank account, but by the size of your heart.
